analysis.title: Europe Open - Hang in there
key_insights: BoJ held rates at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote (Takata dissenting), in line with expectations, and said underlying inflation had reached its 2% target. Ueda said the bank will judge a rate hike at each meeting, including December.
Citi's base case is a 25bp BoJ hike in December, with +20bp currently priced. The desk says the ETF sales pace change starting Jan 2027 avoids stacking two tightening actions in December.
BoJ raised its 2027 core CPI forecast to 2.6% from 2.4%. Core ex-energy is 0.1pp higher for 2027 and 2028. GDP is raised for 2026 and lowered for 2027.

Weaker tech sentiment after misses from Amazon and Intel pushed equities lower. Kospi fell 3.4%, Nikkei 2%, Nasdaq futures 1.9% and S&P e-minis 1%. HSI rose about 2% on its negative correlation with AI sentiment.
Treasuries held gains on safe haven flows. JGB 15-year yields rose 7.6bp after the BoJ, and the UST rally was helped by domestic receiving flows in Tokyo before duration selling midday.

Citi expects the ECB to hike 25bp in December, and possibly in March, with limited conviction beyond that because of the coming change of ECB leadership. The new President (de Cos or Knot) is expected by Nov 13.
USDJPY was flat after the BoJ. The Citi trader expects downside pressure, with rallies toward 158.00-50 attracting supply.
Month-end FX hedge rebalancing points to buying of all major currencies and selling of USD, and the size has grown because US equities did better this week.
Risk-beta USD put vols are repricing higher as equities fall and USTs rally. EURUSD is outperforming on the USD put side, while vols sold off overnight on vol unwinds.
Oil was marginally higher. Iran said it received a letter from US VP JD Vance but signalled no change in peace deal terms. Qatari mediators have returned to Tehran for US-Iran talks.

Citi's US Midterms guide (election Nov 3) says the Senate is too close to call and narrowing House battlegrounds favor a Democratic retake. A Democratic sweep is increasingly priced in, and macro is likely to dominate near term.
Eurozone data due: German HICP expected at 2.9% YoY vs 3.3% prior. Citi economists expect Eurozone HICP at 3.9% YoY with core at 2.5%. Eurozone Q3 GDP is seen slowing to 0.2% QoQ from 0.6%.
Banrep is expected to hike 25bp to 12.50% (18:00 GMT), following a surprise 25bp hike in September.

sector_views.rationale: Misses from Amazon and Intel weighed on regional equity indices again, and tech sentiment is weak.

earnings_insights: Amazon and Intel earnings misses were cited as weighing on regional equity indices. The note gives no EPS or revenue figures.

The upward revision supports the case for further hikes.
The market prices most of a 25bp hike.
Expected to ease. Inflation is expected to rise further in Germany in early 2027 as gas passes through to HICP.
Citi economists' forecast for headline, with core unchanged.
Slower growth, though excluding Ireland the underlying pace is roughly unchanged, slightly below the ECB's 0.3% forecast.
Citi is in line with consensus. ECI is a read on labor cost pressures.
Bloomberg consensus expects a modest recovery. The prior YoY was 1.4%.
Lower fuel prices from government measures are the main driver. Citi's proxy shows a 10.7% MoM drop in pump fuel prices.
Citi economists expect a final 25bp hike.
Supported by net exports, investment and AI demand.
Monthly activity points to further recovery.
Upside risks from industrial production and AI exports.
Export growth is expected to slow.

Ueda flagged a risk that the price trend goes above 2%.
The change of ECB leadership limits visibility on policy beyond March.
Midterm outcome uncertainty, with the Senate too close to call.
Stacking BoJ tightening actions in December could amplify market volatility.
